title: ICT for Development
description: What ICT is and how it drives development, the digital divide, applications of ICT, the design–reality gap model, developmental informatics and big data, participatory design, and ICT4D technologies such as e-health, e-government and GIS.

topics.title: ICT and the Digital Divide
topics.summary: ICT is the diverse set of tools used to transmit, store, create, share or exchange information, from radio and telephones to the Internet, cloud and AI, and it is broader than IT. Its benefits are unevenly spread, creating a digital divide, and its developmental characteristics make it an enabler of economic growth, social development and good governance.
subtopics: Definitions of ICT and the technologies included
ICT versus IT; components of ICT
Importance to business and the challenges ICT creates
The digital age and the digital divide
Developmental characteristics of ICTs
ICTs for economic growth, social development and governance; factors affecting ICT-driven development

topics.title: Applications of ICT
topics.summary: ICT is applied through teleconferencing, video conferencing and tele-presence, which adds telecommunication networking, tele-computing, messaging and information search to video conferencing. ICT gadgets such as radio, television, VSAT, GSM and ATMs change education, industry, the military, entertainment, medicine, finance, government, homes, agriculture and business.
subtopics: Teleconferencing and video conferencing
Tele-presence and how it differs from video conferencing
ICT-based gadgets
Impacts on education, industry, politics and the military
Impacts on entertainment, medical science, finance and public sector management
Impacts on home electronics, agriculture and business

topics.title: The Design–Reality Gap
topics.summary: The design–reality gap model measures the gap between a project's design assumptions and the reality on the ground, from 0 (no gap) to 10 (radical gap), along the seven ITPOSMO dimensions. Large gaps point to the problems to fix, and the model explains why many e-government and big data projects in developing countries partly or totally fail.
subtopics: What the design–reality gap is
The seven ITPOSMO dimensions
The Colombian public-sector big data example
Collecting data: interviews and group discussions
Rating, summing and interpreting the gap scores
Importance to e-government managers

topics.title: Developmental Informatics and Big Data
topics.summary: Development informatics studies the role of ICTs in sustainable socio-economic development, linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Big data offers new, cheap, real-time sources (digital footprints) and analytics, with five characteristics, but faces limits such as the Lucas critique, access gaps and skills shortages.
subtopics: Development informatics and the SDGs
The two-fold core of big data
Nowcasting and the Lucas critique
Goals of ICT4D
Five characteristics of big data
Opportunities and challenges for development

topics.title: Participatory Design and ICT4D Technologies
topics.summary: Participatory design involves users and stakeholders in designing a product, guided by principles of user focus, mutual learning, empowerment, inclusiveness and respect. Key ICT4D technologies include e-health (EHRs, m-health, sensors, telehealth), e-government, information infrastructures, GIS and digital archiving.

e-Health: EHRs, m-health, sensors and telehealth; barriers
e-Government and the factors affecting it
